m_scope: Closed trades and funding fees only. The program has no stop-loss by default, so apart from a delisting exit or a liquidation it does not close a losing position on its own. A loss shows up in these numbers only once a position is closed at a loss; until then it stays in an open position. Open positions are not in these numbers — you can see them on the “Open positions” screenshot exactly as the dashboard shows them.
m_trades_note: The dashboard's “Total N Trades” and Win Rate also count funding-fee entries. Here funding is counted separately, which is why the two sets of numbers differ.
m_zero_policy: A trade closed at exactly 0 counts as neither profit nor loss.
chart_note: Daily sum of closed-trade P&L and funding fees, added up. This is not the account balance curve, and the paper loss of an open position does not appear in it.

hiw_desc: What the program is, where it runs, how the developer is paid, and how you can check it yourself.
hiw_lead: JaviD Future Bot is a desktop program for USDⓈ-M perpetual futures. It is made and distributed by one independent developer.
hiw_s1_p: On your Windows or macOS computer. You create an API key on your exchange, enter it in the program's Settings, and the program places orders from your PC. The key is stored on your computer. Your PC has to stay on while it trades.
hiw_s2_p: Three quant strategies watch the symbols you select and open and add to positions by their rules. Default safeguards in V19.7: no new entries on symbols listed less than 90 days ago; after 3 new entries on the same symbol and side within 24 hours, new entries are blocked until 48 hours after the first (adding to an open position is not counted); and a delisting filter. There is no stop-loss by default; an optional 60% hard stop can be switched on.
hiw_s3_p1: The program is free: no subscription, no license key, no paid tier.
hiw_s3_p2: Where the exchange runs a broker program, it shares part of the trading fee you already pay with the developer. Your fee is the same either way.
hiw_s3_l1: Bitget — 12% of the trading fee you already pay, for new and existing accounts.
hiw_s3_l2: Binance — only for accounts opened after the developer joined the program. If you already have a Binance account, the developer earns nothing from your trading. Please do not open a second Binance account to change that; Binance prohibits it.
hiw_s3_l3: Bybit and OKX — the program carries the exchange's broker or referral identifiers where available. Your fee does not change.
hiw_s3_p3: The sign-up links on this website are the exchanges' plain registration pages, not referral links.
hiw_s4_h: The conflict of interest, stated plainly
hiw_s4_p: Being paid per trade gives the developer a reason to want more trades. The developer sets the entry rules and defaults that ship with each build, and the advanced strategy settings are password-locked. Those defaults also include a rule that cuts trades: at most 3 new entries per symbol in 24 hours. Your settings are stored in a file on your computer, and the developer cannot see or change them while the program runs. In Shadow Mode you can watch how often it trades before any money is involved.
hiw_s5_l1: Compare the SHA-256 checksum of your download with the one on the download page.
hiw_s5_l2: While it runs, list the hosts it connects to (Resource Monitor on Windows, lsof -i -P on macOS).
hiw_s5_l3: Watch the live account's dashboard — hourly captures here, and the YouTube live stream.
hiw_s5_l4: Run Shadow Mode for as long as you like before connecting real funds.
hiw_s6_p: The source code is not public. The Windows and macOS builds are packaged and obfuscated, so you cannot read the strategy code. If you need to read every line of a bot before using it, open-source projects such as Freqtrade or Hummingbot are better suited to that.

g_title: How to use JaviD Future Bot — setup with screenshots
g_desc: Step-by-step setup with real screenshots: enter and save your API key, set the investment amount, entry mode and leverage, select all symbols and save, then press Start Trading.
g_lead: Screenshots from the actual program (Bitget build, English UI, fake placeholder keys, nothing connected). The other exchange builds use the same tabs and buttons; differences are listed at the bottom.
g_s0_p: Download the build for your exchange and unzip it. On Windows run JaviD_Future_Bot.exe; on macOS open start.command. The program opens in your browser at a local address on your own PC. Close the first-run welcome window to reach the tabs.
g_s1_t: Settings — enter your API key and click Save
g_s1_p: Open the Settings tab. Paste the Access Key and Secret Key you created on the exchange (Bitget and OKX also need the Passphrase) and click Save. Test Connection next to it checks the key. Keep withdrawals disabled on the key.
g_s2_p: Under Investment Mode (Margin Ratio per Entry), pick how much of your balance each entry uses: margin per entry = balance ÷ 100, 200, 300, 500 or 700. Normal (÷ 500) is the default; a larger number means smaller entries. Clicking a mode applies it. (The Binance build offers Aggressive, Normal and Stable.)
g_s3_p: Under Entry Mode, choose Conservative (single) — the first matching strategy only — or Multi Mode, which rotates through the strategies. The choice applies immediately.
g_s4_p: Under Leverage, choose 3x, 5x, 10x or 15x. New installs start at 10x. The setting applies to the next new entry; open positions keep their leverage. Higher leverage brings liquidation closer.
g_s5_p: Open the Symbol Selection tab and click Select All (or tick only the symbols you want).
g_s6_p: Click Save Selection. The program then loads candle data for every selected symbol; wait until it finishes.
g_s7_p: Click Start Trading at the top right. If Shadow Mode (in the Operations Console on the right, off by default) is on, it trades with a virtual balance. With Shadow Mode off, a confirmation of the leverage and margin summary appears before real orders start.
g_tip_h: Recommended: watch in Shadow Mode first
g_tip_p: Switch on Shadow Mode in the Operations Console before pressing Start Trading and let it run for a few days. You see the same decisions on live prices without real orders.
g_diff_bitget: Bitget: Access Key, Secret Key and Passphrase; the key needs futures read and trade permission.
g_diff_okx: OKX: API Key, Secret Key and Passphrase; the account mode must be “Futures mode” with USDT in the Trading account. (Download preparing.)
g_diff_binance: Binance: Access Key and Secret Key only. Investment modes are Aggressive, Normal and Stable.
g_diff_bybit: Bybit: API Key and API Secret, no passphrase. The account must be a Unified Trading Account with USDT in it, and the key needs Read-Write with Contract orders and positions. Bybit keys are 18 characters long — that is normal.

rk_desc: Losses, leverage and liquidation, costs, backtest limits, copy-trading differences, API key responsibility and how the figures on this site are calculated.
rk_lead: Read this before downloading or connecting funds.
rk_1_h: You can lose your entire capital
rk_1_p: Leveraged futures can lose your entire capital. A position can be liquidated, and losses can exceed what you expected when you opened it.
rk_2_h: Leverage and no stop-loss by default
rk_2_p: Higher leverage brings liquidation closer. By default the program has no stop-loss, so a position can stay in a deep loss for a long time; the optional 60% hard stop limits that at the cost of realizing the loss.
rk_3_p: The live figures come from one account over a limited period. Another account, period, symbol set or setting can give a very different result, including losses.
rk_4_p: Backtests replay history with assumptions: price data, fees, funding, slippage and which symbols existed. They can be wrong in ways live trading reveals. Backtests are never combined with live records on this site.
rk_5_p: Trading fees, funding fees and slippage reduce results. Funding can be paid or received while a position is open.
rk_6_p: A follower's result differs from the leader's because of delay, size, fees and profit share.
rk_7_p: You create, store and revoke the key. Keep withdrawal permission off and restrict the key to your IP where possible. Anyone with the key and secret can trade your account.
rk_8_p: The program, your PC, your network or the exchange can fail or behave unexpectedly. Keep the PC on and check positions on the exchange itself.
rk_9_h: How the figures here are calculated
rk_9_p: Realized P&L = closed-trade P&L plus funding fees from the program's trade records. Open positions are excluded. “Closed in profit” counts trades with P&L above 0. Dates are Korea time. One account is the whole sample. Because there is no stop-loss by default, a losing position does not appear in these figures until it is closed.
rk_10_p: The developer can receive part of the trading fee you pay through exchange broker programs. See How it works.
rk_11_p: Nothing on this site is investment advice or a recommendation to trade. You decide and you are responsible for the outcome.
faq_desc: Answers about cost, API key safety, losses, Shadow Mode, operating systems, live records and copy trading.
a1: Yes. There is no subscription or paid tier. The developer can receive part of the trading fee you already pay through exchange broker programs — details on How it works.
q2: Does the program need withdrawal permission?
a2: No. Create the key with futures trading only and keep withdrawals disabled. If the exchange allows it, restrict the key to your PC's IP address.
a3: Yes. Leveraged futures can lose your entire capital, and there is no stop-loss by default. Start in Shadow Mode and only use money you can afford to lose.
q4: Can I try it without an exchange account or API key?
a4: Shadow Mode runs the strategies on live prices with a virtual balance. To place real orders you need an account and an API key.
q5: Which systems does it run on?
a5: Windows and macOS. Android is on hold and there is no iOS version. Your computer has to stay on while it trades.
q6: Why does Windows or macOS warn me when I open it?
a6: The program is made by an individual developer and is not signed with a paid code-signing certificate, so the operating system cannot verify the publisher. The download page shows how to open it and how to check the file's SHA-256 checksum.
q7: What do the live figures on this site mean?
a7: They come from one real Binance account: hourly screenshots of its dashboard and figures computed from its own trade records (closed trades plus funding fees, open positions excluded). With no stop-loss by default, a losing position stays open instead of being closed, so it appears on the open-positions screenshot, not in the figures. One account over a limited period is the whole sample.
a8: Not at the moment. An earlier backtest was withdrawn after a counting error was found. A new one will be shown only after verification, separately from live records.
q9: How is copy trading different from the program?
a9: Copy trading runs on the exchange's page and nothing is installed. Your result differs from the leader's. Bitget and Bybit profiles are listed on the copy-trading page; Binance and OKX are preparing.
a10: By email at support@javidtrading.com, in the Telegram community, or on the community board.

pv_desc: What this website records: download events without IP address or user agent, community board posts, and nothing from the program itself.
pv_1_p: The program runs on your computer. Your API key and settings are stored there. The program does not send your key, balance or trades to the developer.
pv_2_p: When you download a build, the download server on that exchange's subdomain (bg., bn. or bb.javidtrading.com) records one row: the time, the platform (Windows or macOS), the country reported by the network, the referring site's host name, UTM campaign tags, the page you came from on this site, a coarse client type (browser, bot, script) and the browser's Sec-Fetch-Site value. Your IP address and full user agent are not stored. We use this to count downloads and see which channels work.
pv_3_p: This site keeps where you arrived from in your browser's session storage (cleared when the tab closes) so a download can be attributed to that channel.
pv_4_p: The name and message you post are stored. For private posts a salted hash of your password is stored, not the password.
pv_5_p: If you write to us, we keep the conversation to answer you.
pv_6_p: The site is served by Cloudflare. Fonts are loaded from jsDelivr. Exchange and YouTube links take you to those services under their own policies.
